question:
(a) State the law of radioactive decay.
(b) Obtain the expression $N = N_{0}e^{-\lambda t}$.
(c) Explain the physical meaning of decay constant $\lambda$.

options.A:
(a) Decay rate is directly proportional to number of decayed nuclei: $dN/dt=+\lambda N$.
(b) Thus $N=N_0e^{\lambda t}$.
(c) $\lambda$ is the average mass of a nucleus.
options.B:
(a) Radioactive disintegration rate is proportional to the number $N$ of undecayed nuclei: $\frac{dN}{dt}=-\lambda N$.
(b) Integrating $\frac{dN}{N}=-\lambda dt$ from $N_0$ to $N$ gives $\ln(N/N_0)=-\lambda t$, hence $N=N_0e^{-\lambda t}$.
(c) $\lambda$ is the probability of decay per unit time for a nucleus and is characteristic of the isotope.
options.C:
(a) $dN/dt=-N/\lambda$.
(b) $N=N_0-\lambda t$.
(c) $\lambda$ is the number of protons in the nucleus.
options.D:
(a) Decay rate is constant: $dN/dt=-\lambda$.
(b) $N=N_0/2^t$.
(c) $\lambda$ depends only on the amount of sample.
